r0.why: First billion years, gigayear/Ga, 4.55 to about 3.5 Gya (1); all of the Hadean and about a third of the Archean (2).

r1.why: Accretion from solar nebula (3), 4.54 billion years (9), 50 to 100 million years and debate (10), June 2023 three million years (11), ~3 and ~70 million years (12).

r2.why: Intense impacts, 0.63 Earth masses, Theia Mars-sized co-orbital from L4, 0.032 Ga, magma oceans and core formation (4); late veneer delivery of water and volatiles (5).

r3.why: Hydrogen/helium primary atmosphere to reductant secondary one (3); end-Hadean cooling, crust, superocean, lava planet to ocean planet, earliest life soon after (6).

r4.why: Little crust survives, 4.404 Gya zircon in Jack Hills conglomerate (7); Isua and earliest supracrustal terrains about 3.8 Gya near peak Late Heavy Bombardment (8).

r5.why: Life in oceans within first billion years (13), at least 3.5 billion years (15), graphite in Greenland and 4.1-billion-year zircons (16), November 2020 atmosphere report (17).
